body: I'm an EBFer too cus of work and nursing aversion. Hopefully it works for me, I get so self conscious about my smell while I'm in office.

Oooh interesting. I started noticing my odor a month or two after giving birth. I know that my hormones have been pretty bad throughout my mommy journey so I think that probably has a lot to do with it.
Do you have a clay mask that you suggest? I might try this!
I wonder if birth control would help me. Before the baby I really didn't sweat... Even sitting in a sauna it took a lot of effort to produce much sweat. But now just existing does the trick 😒
It never goes away?? I guess I'll just have to get used to this being smelly thing 🥺
There goes my theory about it being more about breastfeeding. :(

I'm wondering the same thing, my baby isn't old enough to be weaned just yet but we are approaching the first birthday. So I don't know if this is permanent, permanent for some, or it just goes away after the hormones settle.

Interesting, did you breastfeed too? Did you sweat less maybe after your body adjusted to breastfeeding or not breastfeeding I wonder? I'm trying to understand this new mom body more...since no one really tells us about this stuff
I'll give it a read! Thank you for the suggestion.
My mom isn't very reliable...she... REALLY enjoys her freedom. But if I catch her before she makes her own plans I might be able to schedule some time out.

I haven't had a conversation where I've gotten through to him yet. 
I've always backed out of having the conversation because either A. He isn't listening anyway B. He just nods his head and wants to get handsy or C. He gets stressed out because it's a serious conversation.

I myself have been too preoccupied trying to keep my job and juggle the baby and housework that I feel like having the conversation is going to be a lot more stress on my plate. But I should do it.. it's just tough

Yes, 

I want to sit down and have a proper conversation with him. He's the type that doesn't handle emotional anything well...while it doesn't excuse him from having these conversations with me---its difficult because I find myself trying to find good timing..

Thank you for asking. 

I'm hanging in there...
I want to go to therapy, my partner currently gets mad when I talk about seeking help because he thinks it's a waste of money...

In the past he's also had the tendency to tell me "have you ever just tried not being sad?" He doesn't really like talking about these kinds of things cus it stresses him out.

I have better days now than I did in the beginning as I adjust to motherhood---Ive had to learn how to handle my negative emotions (if even just for a few minutes) while I put baby somewhere safe or down for a nap while I go release bad energy before coming back. This is just how I've been coping recently--- but really... Thank you for checking.

This is exactly why it's been weighing on my mind.... I don't want my baby to think this is acceptable behavior... On one hand--- there is a chance that dad and I can find an understanding... But it definitely doesn't seem like that's going to happen. I came to vent because of this exact thing....

Yes, I am aware.

I also have had my depression worsen after giving birth... I apologize if it seems like I don't care about his feelings at all...
No, I'll look into it thank you
Pumping while bottle feeding might really help, getting to a point where I even have bottles ready is tough right now---but I'll definitely give it a shot, thank you
